Getting started
Welcome to this workshop!






Before you start



Make sure you have the following:

R
RStudio
GitHub account (free)



In this workshop you will learn to:

Effectively collaborate with remote peers on a data-science project using git and GitHub.
Track changes and version control
Open-source principles
Scientific and technical publishing

title: What is Git?
text: Git is a tool that helps you track and manage changes to your files, making it easy to collaborate with others and keep a clear history of your work.

title: What is Git?
text:
Second, some practice
I have created a sandbox repository for you to practice git commands.
link to the repo

Step 1: Clone the repository to your local
Use the terminal to clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/lessardlab/Workshop_March_25.git


Step 2: Create a new branch
git checkout -b my_branch_name


Step 3: Continue the story

Edit the _keep_the_story_going.md file and add a new line to the story.



Step 4: Add and commit your changes
git add _keep_the_story_going.md or git add .
git commit -m "Add a new line to the story"


Step 5: Push your changes to the remote repository
git push origin my_branch_name


Step 6: Create a pull request
Go to the repository on GitHub and create a pull request to merge your changes into the main branch.


Step 7: Review and merge the pull request
Review the changes and merge the pull request.


Step 8: Update your local repository
git checkout main
git pull origin main
Optional: delete the source branch.
git branch -d my_branch_name

title: What is Quarto?
text: Quarto is an open-source publishing system that seamlessly integrates code, text, and visuals into dynamic, reproducible documents. It’s designed to streamline your workflow, combining elements of Markdown, code execution (in R, Python, Julia, and more), and modern publishing formats into one intuitive toolkit.

title: What is Quarto?
text:
How Does Quarto Work?
You write your document in plain Markdown with embedded code blocks. Quarto processes this into polished outputs, embedding your results, plots, tables, and interactive components seamlessly.

title: What is Quarto?
section: How to collaborate in a Quarto project?
text:
How to collaborate in a Quarto project?
By combining Git and Quarto, you can collaborate in creating and publishing technical reports, papers, dashboards, books, and websites.
